When the News Is Too Much

For when the news has taken over your attention and your mood. It fixes two times a day to look, turns the notifications off, swaps the feed for two sources, puts one thing you can actually do in front of you, and stops an hour before bed.

News · Anxiety · Boundaries · Stress · 9 items · whenever you need it

The checklist

  • Pick two times a day to look and stick to them — the rest of the day does not need updating.
  • Read it rather than watch it — text lets you stop, and video keeps deciding for you.
  • Turn off notifications from news apps entirely — you do not need interrupting by the world.
  • Choose two sources and leave the feed alone — a feed is built to keep you there, not to inform you.
  • Do one thing that is actually in your reach — donate, write, show up, or help one person.
  • Stop reading an hour before bed — the night is not when anything gets solved.
  • Notice when you are refreshing rather than reading — refreshing is anxiety, not information.
  • Talk to one person about it out loud — carrying it silently makes it feel bigger than it is.
  • Let yourself be uninformed for a day — the world does not require your constant attention.

Use this checklist Free account: tick items off and keep each day's record.

How to use it

Run through it whenever you need it, honestly and without scoring yourself. A checklist is a way of noticing, not a test: an item you cannot tick is information about the day, not a verdict on you. Over a few weeks the pattern of what gets ticked and what does not says more than any single pass.

With a free Theraglee account the checklist remembers each pass, so you can look back. Without one, you can still read it here and keep your own copy.
